appraisal_events.evidence: « — Ah ! dans ces conditions, il vaut mieux que la duchesse ne fasse rien, dit Mme de Parme. — Naturellement, conclut le duc. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The duc's campaign against the favor succeeds: the princesse withdraws her request herself, and his curt « Naturellement » ratifies the refusal without conceding anything, leaving her to change the subject.

appraisal_events.evidence: « — Oh ! ce n’est pas grave, ce n’est que la septième fois, dit le duc qui, ayant dû lui-même renoncer à la politique, aimait assez les insuccès électoraux des autres. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator glosses the duc's witticism about the general's seventh electoral defeat by tracing it to his own abandoned political career, so the mot that ridicules the general simultaneously exposes the duc's petty relish for others' failures.

status_effects.explanation: He wins the exchange outright: the request is abandoned by the petitioner herself and he closes the matter with a single word.
The narrator's aside makes his cruel joke a symptom of his own political failure, lowering how he is judged even as he dominates the conversation.
She gives up her request under pressure and then visibly changes the subject, conceding the ground to the duc.

She is settled about rather than consulted, and the agreed conclusion is that her intercession with the general would be worthless, though the arrangement is framed so as to spare her reputation for amiability.
He is the butt of the scene: a seventh electoral defeat and a coarse joke that reduces his consolation to getting his wife pregnant again.

ambiguities: The general is named only in the immediately preceding context (« général de Monserfeuil »); within this passage he appears solely as « ce pauvre général », so the identification rests on prior-context resolution and he is not on the reference sheet.

The closing line « Il s’est consolé en voulant faire un nouvel enfant à sa femme » carries no speech tag; read here as the duc continuing his own mockery, but it could belong to another speaker, which would shift part of the ridicule away from him.
